conventions.convention: Concordance annuli have oriented boundary −K₀ at the lower end and K₁ at the upper end, are proper, and have product endpoint collars. TOP concordances must be locally flat.
K† is the image under the fixed orientation-reversing reflection, with the induced knot orientation then reversed.
PL concordance uses PL locally flat annuli and PL product collars; its definition asserts no identification with smooth or TOP concordance.
General arc unknotting concerns the image. Pointwise terminal parametrization requires α(s)=(p,s) near the source endpoints.
Slice genera minimize over connected compact orientable proper surfaces in the standard four-ball; genus satisfies χ=1−2g and includes zero. This definition assumes countable choice.
A metabolizer is an integral primitive rank-half direct summand on which the entire bilinear Seifert pairing vanishes. Rank zero is allowed. Knot-derived Seifert pairings retain full AC.
The four-dimensional intersection formula uses the boundary orientation of the standard oriented four-ball, positive-meridian linking, rational cycles and collared rational bounding chains.

load_bearing.statement: Assume full AC. For a locally flat proper slice disk D and a connected oriented Seifert surface F of its boundary, the collar-adjusted closed surface F∪D bounds a compact connected oriented locally flat three-manifold R in B⁴, with a two-sided ambient product neighborhood aligned with the positive Seifert push-off.

Assume full AC. If a smooth oriented knot bounds a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball, the positive-push Seifert lattice of every specified connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface is metabolic.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Smooth concordances K₀∼K₁ and J₀∼J₁ imply a smooth concordance K₀#J₀∼K₁#J₁. The same implication holds for locally flat topological concordances.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot K has K#K† bounding a smooth proper disk in the standard four-ball whose squared radial function is Morse on its interior with critical indices only 0 and 1.

Assume AC. For disjoint finite rational boundary 1-cycles α,β represented by oriented knots and rational bounding 2-chains P,Q with standard product collars and general-position interiors, P·Q=lk(α,β).
For an integral bilinear form on a free abelian group H of rank 2g, a g-dimensional rational isotropic subspace L gives a rank-g direct summand H∩L on which the integral form vanishes.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. A smooth oriented knot bounds a smooth proper disk in the unit four-ball if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 obtains an annulus-adapted tube from tubular neighborhoods of the doubled torus and core, then says: “At each level this glues two three-balls” and “the gluing is independent of the interval parameter.” The preceding construction has not explicitly made that tube level-preserving in the original product coordinates. A short smooth local argument closes this: along the vertical core, height restricts submersively to the annulus, permitting a sufficiently small levelwise strip and levelwise normal disks. State this choice, or justify replacement by such a tube, before concluding that the glued ambient manifold is S³×I.
